questions: Have you had similar sudden involuntary movements before this examination?
Are these movements reliably triggered by light touch or brushing of your face or scalp?
Do they also occur spontaneously without anyone touching you?
Do you remain fully conscious and able to respond during the movements?
Do you remember everything that happens during each episode?
Does each movement last only a few seconds?
Does the movement consistently affect the same side of your body?
Does it begin in your face and then spread to your arm or other body parts?
Have you ever had an episode in which you became unresponsive or lost awareness?
Have you ever had prolonged confusion or unusual sleepiness after one of these episodes?
Have you ever bitten your tongue or lost bladder control during an episode?
Are you unusually sensitive to sudden sounds or unexpected touch, causing you to jerk?
Can you voluntarily suppress or prevent the movement when you feel it starting?
Did these episodes begin during childhood or adolescence?
Have the episodes become more frequent or severe over time?
Have you ever been diagnosed with epilepsy or another neurologic disorder?
Have you had a prior stroke, head injury, brain infection, or brain tumor?
Does anyone in your family have epilepsy or similar stimulus-triggered movements?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder with functional (psychogenic) myoclonus/nonepileptic attacks

ALTERNATIVE 1: Cortical myoclonus without a detectable scalp-EEG correlate

ALTERNATIVE 2: Propriospinal or segmental myoclonus

ALTERNATIVE 3: Startle syndrome (hyperekplexia)
